problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$

feedback.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}19 \\ 33 \\ 23\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{4}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}19 \\ 33 \\ 23\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}32 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}304 \\ 33 \\ 23\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}72 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}720 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}72 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}720 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{72\cdot 2-0\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 72\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}720 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{144}[\begin{aligned}1\,440 \\ 720\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
